## Second labeler agreement: nodegoat-a3118b6

A second labeller, a separate model session rather than a person, labelled 20 threats from the primary sheet without seeing its labels. That is a weaker check than a second human. Agreement is the share of threats with the same label.

- **supported (y/n)**: 16/20 agree (80.0%), Cohen's kappa 0.47
- **matchesExpected**: not labelled by the second labeller (the column is blank on every row, not "matches nothing"); match agreement and kappa are omitted
- **evidenceCorrect, exact cell**: 17/20 agree (85.0%)
- **Supported disagreements**: threat-23, threat-72, threat-115, threat-131

## Definitions

- **Recall**: expected threats matched by at least one generated threat labelled `supported = y`, over expected threats. A generated threat is matched when its `matchesExpected` cell lists the expected id; a blank cell means it matches none. A match on an unsupported row does not recall the item (it counts toward Unsupported instead).
- **Unsupported**: generated threats labeled `supported = n` (the cited code does not support the claim), over all generated threats. Lower is better.
- **Evidence accuracy**: evidence items judged correct, over evidence items cited, summed across all threats (from each `evidenceCorrect` cell, e.g. 2/3).
- **Cost**: total model spend for the run as recorded by the pipeline, at the model profile above, with every developer question skipped.
- **All repos** pools the counts; it is not an average of the per-repo percentages.

## Method

- **Answer key before the run.** `eval/expected/nodegoat-a3118b6.yaml` lists 19 expected
  threats for OWASP NodeGoat, written before any run was labelled. It is still a draft,
  not verified by a second person.
- **Pinned code.** NodeGoat at `c5cb68a7084e4ae7dcc60e6a98768720a81841e8`, level 2, demo
  profile, every developer question skipped.
- **Labelling rules.** These are the settled rules in
  `eval/review/pending-evaluation-requirements.md`. Every threat, hidden ones included, is
  judged against the pinned source, not its title. Recall counts only a match on a row
  labelled `supported = y` (R1).
- **Six-way scheme.** The second labeller used confirmed_useful, predicted_correct,
  predicted_wrong, unsupported, too_generic and misclassified. The primary sheet records
  `supported`, `matchesExpected` and `evidenceCorrect`, so agreement above is computed on
  `supported` and `evidenceCorrect` only.

## NodeGoat runs

From `eval/review/nodegoat-a3118b6-report.md`. Every run is NodeGoat at `c5cb68a`, and
every row is labelled against the pinned source.

| run | threats | visible | recall | visible recall | unsupported | visible unsupported | evidence acc | script-reads-cookie claims (unsupported/total) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| after-fix (corrected) | 109 | 11 | 12/19 | 4/19 | 23/109 | 3/11 | 87/111 | 6/7 |
| c8dd73f | 118 | 16 | 16/19 | 7/19 | 28/118 | 3/16 | 97/117 | 11/12 |
| 7a0fb27 | 98 | 35 | 13/19 | 8/19 | 23/98 | 10/35 | 92/102 | 6/7 |
| f64cfa8 | 89 | 24 | 14/19 | 7/19 | 25/89 | 4/24 | 93/105 | 5/5 |
| **a3118b6** | 136 | 37 | **17/19** | **10/19** | 32/136 | **4/37** | 127/146 | **0/0** |

**v1 vs v2.** f64cfa8 is the last run on the `threats.v1` prompt. a3118b6 is the first on
`threats.v2`, which adds the HttpOnly cookie rule. Script-reads-cookie claims went from 5/5
unsupported to none. Each run generates a different threat set, and a3118b6 also carries
`b956a3f`, so the recall change is not attributable to the prompt alone. This is one run
per prompt.

Visible recall is from the review report. `score.ts` does not compute it yet
(requirement R2 in `eval/review/pending-evaluation-requirements.md`).

## Gap precision: not yet measured

`eval/labels/nodegoat-a3118b6.gaps.csv` has 39 rows (threats whose cited evidence is only
control gaps), and 0 of them are labelled. Gap precision is
predicted_correct / (predicted_correct + predicted_wrong), overall and visible only. It
will be reported here once every row has a `gapLabel`. No number is given until then.

## Second-labeller disagreements (supported)

The second labeller was a separate Claude Fable 5.1 session. It saw only CLAUDE.md, the
blank sample, the saved result and the pinned NodeGoat source (commit `092c3d0`). The
sample is n = 20, stratified with a fixed seed (`scripts/eval/sampleSecond.ts`).

| Threat | Primary | Second | Primary reason | Second reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| threat-23 | n | y (predicted_correct) | Headers really are missing, but clickjacking fails: the session cookie has no SameSite, so a cross-site iframe is logged out; the CSP half assumes an injection it does not establish. | helmet is a dependency but server.js:10 comments out the require and :45 the frameguard call, so no frame-protection header is set. |
| threat-72 | y | n (too_generic) | Mongo connection exhaustion makes memo routes fail through next(err); conditional on network access. | A database going away taking its reads and writes with it is true of any web app; memos.js:25-26 forwards the error like every handler. |
| threat-115 | n | y (misclassified) | Same as threat-23: headers missing, but clickjacking fails and the CSP half assumes an injection. | The gap is real (server.js:10 and :51), but missing headers are A02 Security Misconfiguration, not A05 Injection. |
| threat-131 | y | n (too_generic) | Unauthenticated tutorial routes have no throttle or cache; exhaustion is a degree question. | tutorial.js:8 and :31 render static pages; being requestable in a loop is true of any web app. |

Two disagreements (threat-23, threat-115) are about the claimed impact, not the missing
control. Both labellers agree the headers are absent. The other two are about whether a
generic availability threat counts as supported.

## Seeded benchmark

From `eval/bench/report.md` (commit `1d3237a`, three seeded repositories, no model called):

| Mode | TP/FP/FN | Precision | Recall | False-gap rate | Deterministic |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| detectors | 15/1/0 | 93.8% | 100.0% | 1/17 (5.9%) | yes |
| detectors+semgrep | 18/1/0 | 94.7% | 100.0% | 1/17 (5.9%) | yes |

The one false gap is `m-ctl-cross-pkg-owner`: a cross-package guard with an uninformative
name. The seeded apps were written with the detectors in view, so 100% recall is an upper
bound, not an estimate for real repositories.

## Test suite

From `docs/testing.md` (commit `1d3237a`): 92 test files, 3,769 tests (3,768 passed, 1
skipped). Coverage over `src/` is 96.01% statements, 89.49% branches, 94.75% functions and
96.83% lines. The skipped test makes paid model calls and runs only with a key.

## Remaining false positives

These are the visible unsupported threats in a3118b6, from the review report, left as they
are for now:

- t70: marked 0.3.5 advisory bypasses still need a click.
- t73: marked 0.3.5 lacks the ReDoS regex.
- t80: the mongodb advisory's preconditions fail.
- t84: profile self-XSS, and clickjacking of a logged-out frame.

## Caveats

- One real repository (NodeGoat) plus three seeded ones. The results are indicative, not
  general.
- NodeGoat documents its own vulnerabilities in files the model reads, so its recall is
  guided, not blind discovery.
- The primary labels come from one person. The second labeller is a model, not a person,
  and it labelled 20 threats.
- Run-to-run consistency has not been measured yet. The three-run check is planned
  (Prompt I).
